IS: 2058 -1973 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

SHUTTLES FOR PIRN-CHANGING AUTOMATIC 

COTTON LOOMS 

(First Revision) 



(Reaffirmed 2012) 



1- Scope — Dimensional details and other requirements for shuttles for pirn-changing automatic 
cotton looms. 

2. Terminology 

2.1 Left Hand Shuttle — The eye of the shuttle falls on the right-hand side when viewed from the 
weaver's position in front of the loom, 

2.2 Right-Hand Shuttle — The eye of the shuttle falls on the left-hand side when viewed from the 
weaver's position in front of the loom. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As given in Table 1, 

4. Material — Shuttle block conforming to Indian Standard specification for shuttle blocks 
( under preparation ). 

Note — Till such time the standard is published, the material shall be as agreed to between the buyer and the seller. 

5. Shuttle Accessories — Various accessories used in making shuttle shall preferably conform to 
the requirements laid down in Indian Standard specification for accessories for use in shuttles for 
pirn-changing automatic cotton looms ( under preparation ). 

Note — Till such time the standard is published, the accessories shall conform to the requirements as agreed to 
between the buyer and the seller. 

6. Weight — The weight of the shuttle shall be as agreed to between the buyer and the seller 
subject to a tolerance of ± 5 percent. 

7. Manufacture, Workmanship and Finish 

7.1 The timber for the manufacture of the shuttle shall be fully seasoned [see IS : 1141-1973 Code 
of practice for seasoning of timber (first revision ) ]. 

7.2 The shuttle shall be free from knots, cracks and any other visible defect which is likely to affect 
its life or usefulness. 

7.3 The outer surface and the surfaces where the yarn comes into contact shall be finished smooth. 

7.4 The angle of shuttle ( bevel ) shall normally be 90°. 

7.5 If agreed to between the buyer and the seller, the shuttles made of uncompressed wood shall be 
pressure-impregnated with raw linseed oil. 

7.6 If prescribed by the buyer, a fibre washer shall be provided under the tip. 

8. Positioning of Accessories — When the pirn is seated in the shuttle, the centre of pirn shall be 
in line with the centre of the threading eye. 

9. Dropping Test — Drop the shuttle vertically, with one of its tips facing downwards, from a height 
of one metre on a cast iron plate and the tip shall not get blunt. 

10. Marking — Each shuttle shall be marked with the following: 

a) Brand or trade-mark of the manufacturer; 

b) Hand of the shuttle, whether right hand ( R ) or left hand ( L ); and 

c) Code No. to trace the history of production. 

10.1 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Adopted 30 March 1973 



© January 1974, BIS 



Gr 1 



BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS

— 



N t e i Varieties 1, 2 and 3 of the shuttles are normally used for NMM-Ruti looms, Varieties 4 and 5- for Northrop, 

Variety 6 for Picanol, Varieties 7, 3 and 9 for Cooper-Draper and Variety 10 for Cimmco-Sakamoto looms. 

Note 2 — The free space is normally equal to the overall length of the pirn plus 21 to 30, mm. 

Note 3 in case an agreement between the buyer and the seller provides for dimensions other than those specified 

above, they shall be declared and shall be subject to tho tolerances specified above. 

Note 4 The distance between the tip and the jaw cover end depends on the make of the loom In conjunction with 

which the shuttle is to be used. However/it shall be subject to a tolerance of ±0*5 mm. 

Note 5 The location and size of the slots for the midget feeler and the thread cutter depend on the make of the 

loom in conjunction with which the shuttle is to be used.
